date_note: Date is SMBC's announcement of 20 November; SMBC says PLAID reported the intrusion to it on 13 November and the scope on 19 November.
title: SMBC says up to about 14 million customer records leaked via PLAID KARTE breach
summary: SMBC said on 20 November that up to about 14 million records of customer information leaked after unauthorized access to KARTE, a service from its contractor PLAID. The data is dates of birth, category values for age band, gender and whether a phone number is registered, and notice flags; SMBC says it is not linked to names and cannot identify individuals. No impact on assets or transactions is confirmed so far.
plain: Sumitomo Mitsui Bank says up to about 14 million customer records leaked through its contractor PLAID's KARTE service. The bank says names, contact details, account numbers and logins were not included.
exec: Up to about 14 million bank customer records exposed through a vendor's marketing tool.
action: SMBC says it will never ask for passwords or card details by email or phone about this; it urges customers not to open links or attachments in suspicious messages claiming to be from the bank.

sources.name: Rocket Boys Security Measures Lab (Japan), 21 Nov 2026

validation.note: SMBC's own notice (PDF, 20 Nov) read in full by the follow-up desk; it agrees with Cybersecurity.com and Rocket Boys. SMBC says it will report to the relevant authorities. PLAID's 20 Nov notice (plaid.co.jp/news/20261120/) says a vulnerability in internal processing on a public path was exploited in the early hours of 13 November; no attacker named.
